findings.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — The retrieval throttle key is `"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"` (the full URL string), so an attacker who spoofs the referer (see embed_controller.rb:26) can vary the query string on each request under the same allowed host to bypass the 60s per-URL redis dedup and repeatedly drive app/models/topic_embed.rb:22's `PostCreator.new(..., skip_validations: true)`, which explicitly skips SpamRulesEnforcer, enabling unauthenticated mass topic/post creation.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116 — The `--category`/`-c` thor option and its category_id assignment are removed with no deprecation notice, silently breaking existing operator scripts/docs that invoke `thor disqus:import -c CategoryName`.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Switching topic creation to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` drops the previously-passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` for the thread's root post, so migrated topics silently get today's date instead of the original Disqus post date (replies still preserve created_at).

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:8 — EmbedController#best` never sets an explicit HTTP status for any branch (missing embed_url relies on default ActionController::ParameterMissing handling, InvalidAccess relies on default exception mapping, and both 'loading' and the populated topic view return implicit 200), so third-party embedders have no stable, intentionally-designed status-code contract to detect success/loading/error — only the spec's loose `should_not be_success` assertion covers this.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied uniformly, including to the 'loading' placeholder response, so an intermediary cache (CDN/browser) can serve a stale 'still loading' page for up to 60s after the topic actually becomes available, extending the effective wait beyond the client-side 30s reload interval in loading.html.erb.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Access control (`ensure_embeddable`) and the resize protocol's postMessage targetOrigin (app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11) both depend entirely on the optional/mutable `Referer` header with no fallback (e.g. signed token or explicit allow-listed embed_url check), so embedders behind referrer-stripping browser policies/extensions, or hitting the loading page's `document.location.reload()`, can be denied access or lose the resize callback with no documented recovery path.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` validates the postMessage sender by substring containment rather than exact origin equality; it silently rejects legitimate resize messages whenever `discourseUrl` lacks a scheme/trailing slash or otherwise isn't formatted as a strict superstring of `e.origin`, and this externally-loaded script has zero test coverage to pin its behavior.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` requires `discourseUrl` to already end in a trailing slash or the resulting URL is malformed (e.g. `...comembed/best`); this required format for the `discourseUrl`/`discourseEmbedUrl` globals and the `#discourse-comments` element is not documented anywhere in the repo (no README/docs found for third-party integrators).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — The retrieval throttle key is `"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"` (the full URL string), so an attacker who spoofs the referer (see embed_controller.rb:26) can vary the query string on each request under the same allowed host to bypass the 60s per-URL redis dedup and repeatedly drive app/models/topic_embed.rb:22's `PostCreator.new(..., skip_validations: true)`, which explicitly skips SpamRulesEnforcer, enabling unauthenticated mass topic/post creation.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116 — The `--category`/`-c` thor option and its category_id assignment are removed with no deprecation notice, silently breaking existing operator scripts/docs that invoke `thor disqus:import -c CategoryName`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and also deletes the associated `category_id` lookup and passing `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. After this change, `thor disqus:import -c CategoryName` will no longer be accepted by Thor (unknown option) and there is no replacement mechanism or warning in the shown code, so existing scripts/docs using `-c/--category` will break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Switching topic creation to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` drops the previously-passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` for the thread's root post, so migrated topics silently get today's date instead of the original Disqus post date (replies still preserve created_at).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the root post used to be created via `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), ...)`, explicitly preserving the Disqus thread creation time. The diff replaces this with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. Tracing the new call chain: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `TopicEmbed.import` -> `PostCreator.new(user, title: ..., raw: ..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: ...)` and no `created_at` is passed. Since `PostCreator` only sets `post.created_at` when `@opts[:created_at]` is present (see lib/post_creator.rb), the imported topic's first post will default to the current time rather than the Disqus timestamp. The part about replies preserving `created_at` is not shown here, but the regression for the root post date is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:8 — EmbedController#best` never sets an explicit HTTP status for any branch (missing embed_url relies on default ActionController::ParameterMissing handling, InvalidAccess relies on default exception mapping, and both 'loading' and the populated topic view return implicit 200), so third-party embedders have no stable, intentionally-designed status-code contract to detect success/loading/error — only the spec's loose `should_not be_success` assertion covers this.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best the behavior is standard Rails: successful renders (topic view or 'loading') return 200 by default, and error cases are expressed via exceptions (params.require(:embed_url) raises ActionController::ParameterMissing, ensure_embeddable raises Discourse::InvalidAccess). Those exceptions are expected to be mapped to non-2xx responses by the framework/application exception handlers, which is why the spec asserts only `should_not be_success`. The diff does not show any incorrect status being returned or any consumer requirement for a custom status-code contract; the finding is a design preference/speculation rather than a verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied uniformly, including to the 'loading' placeholder response, so an intermediary cache (CDN/browser) can serve a stale 'still loading' page for up to 60s after the topic actually becomes available, extending the effective wait beyond the client-side 30s reload interval in loading.html.erb.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally after the `if topic_id ... else ... render 'loading'` branch. That means the "loading" placeholder response gets the same cache lifetime as the real embed response. Since `loading.html.erb` relies on `document.location.reload()` after 30s, any cache honoring those headers (browser/proxy/CDN) can serve the cached loading page again on reload for up to 60s even if the topic becomes available in the meantime, effectively extending the wait and making the reload less effective.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Access control (`ensure_embeddable`) and the resize protocol's postMessage targetOrigin (app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11) both depend entirely on the optional/mutable `Referer` header with no fallback (e.g. signed token or explicit allow-listed embed_url check), so embedders behind referrer-stripping browser policies/extensions, or hitting the loading page's `document.location.reload()`, can be denied access or lose the resize callback with no documented recovery path.

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` enforces access by requiring `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and raises if the referer is missing or doesn’t match. The `Referer` header is optional and can be stripped by browser/privacy policies, so legitimate embeds can be denied with no alternate validation path (e.g., validating `params[:embed_url]` host or using a signed token). Additionally, the loading page triggers `document.location.reload()` after 30s; that reload is initiated by the iframe document itself, so the subsequent request’s referer will typically be the iframe URL (Discourse host), not the embedding page host, causing `ensure_embeddable` to reject and making the loading flow break. Separately, the embed layout uses `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`, but `targetOrigin` must be an origin (scheme+host+port), not a full referer URL/path; if referer is missing/empty or includes a path, the resize message can fail or throw, making the resize protocol fragile and referer-dependent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` validates the postMessage sender by substring containment rather than exact origin equality; it silently rejects legitimate resize messages whenever `discourseUrl` lacks a scheme/trailing slash or otherwise isn't formatted as a strict superstring of `e.origin`, and this externally-loaded script has zero test coverage to pin its behavior.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` requires `discourseUrl` to already end in a trailing slash or the resulting URL is malformed (e.g. `...comembed/best`); this required format for the `discourseUrl`/`discourseEmbedUrl` globals and the `#discourse-comments` element is not documented anywhere in the repo (no README/docs found for third-party integrators).

adjudication.rationale:
In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the iframe URL is built via string concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`. There is no slash inserted between `discourseUrl` and `embed/best`, so if `discourseUrl` is provided as e.g. `https://forum.example.com` (no trailing `/`), the resulting URL becomes `https://forum.example.comembed/best?...`, which is malformed. The diff does not show any normalization/guarantee that `discourseUrl` always ends with `/`.

The additional claim that this required format (and the required globals/DOM element) is “not documented anywhere in the repo” is not something that can be verified from the diff alone, but the trailing-slash concatenation bug itself is directly evidenced in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:245 — The new public embed route/script (`embed/best`, embed.js) is introduced with no version segment or script version marker, leaving no path to evolve the response shape or postMessage protocol later without breaking already-embedded third-party pages.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new public endpoint (`get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'`) and an embedding script (`embed.js`) that uses a simple postMessage protocol (`type: 'discourse-resize'`). However, the proposed finding is a forward-compatibility/design concern (no explicit API/versioning scheme), not a concrete bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the change. Nothing in the diff demonstrates that the lack of a version segment/marker causes breakage or prevents evolution (the protocol could be extended compatibly, or versioning could be introduced later via query params/headers without being impossible). This is speculative rather than a verifiable problem in the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Replacing the direct PostCreator.new(... category: category_id) call with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]) drops the --category option entirely (also removed from method_option), so imported topics can no longer be placed in a specific category and always land in the default category.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `method_option :category` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes all logic that computed `category_id` from `options[:category]`. The topic creation code is changed from `PostCreator.new(..., category: category_id)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` do not accept or pass through a category. Therefore the `--category` option is no longer supported and imported topics can no longer be placed into a specified category via this task (they will fall back to whatever PostCreator/default category behavior is).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — The same refactor also drops created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) that was previously passed to PostCreator; TopicEmbed.import/PostCreator.new inside import_remote never receives a created_at option, so imported topics lose their original Disqus thread date and are stamped with the import time instead.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the diff changes `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` from creating the topic via `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), ...)` to calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, only `title` is passed through; it calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, ..., doc.content)` with no `created_at`. `TopicEmbed.import` then instantiates `PostCreator` without a `created_at` option. Since `PostCreator` only sets `post.created_at` when `@opts[:created_at]` is present (seen in `lib/post_creator.rb`), the imported post/topic will now be timestamped at import time rather than the Disqus thread's original date.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:37 — Check-then-act race: TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists? is checked, then later app/models/topic_embed.rb:25 TopicEmbed.create! runs inside a transaction; embed_url has a unique index, so two concurrent imports of the same URL (e.g. PollFeed and RetrieveTopic firing close together) will raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique uncaught in the loser, failing that job instead of falling back to the update path.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb) and the code path in TopicEmbed.import first does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction (app/models/topic_embed.rb). With two concurrent imports of the same URL, both can observe `embed.blank?` and both attempt `create!`; the loser will hit the unique constraint and raise an uncaught ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique/StatementInvalid, causing that job/request to fail rather than taking the update path. TopicRetriever.perform_retrieve also does a non-atomic `exists?` check before later calling import logic (lib/topic_retriever.rb), which does not prevent the race.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — add_column :posts, :cook_method with null: false and default: 1 runs as a single blocking statement with no batching; on Postgres versions before 11 this rewrites and locks the entire posts table, causing downtime on a large existing table with no backfill/rollback plan

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` that runs `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` in a single statement. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-null default typically forces a full table rewrite and takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the table for the duration, which can block reads/writes and cause downtime on large `posts` tables. The migration does not use the safer multi-step approach (add nullable/no default, backfill in batches, then set default + NOT NULL), so the operational risk described is directly attributable to this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — revisor.revise! and embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...) are two separate un-transacted operations; if update_column fails after revise! succeeds, content_sha1 stays stale and the same revision is silently reapplied on every later import

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `revisor.revise!(...)` and then separately `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` without wrapping them in a transaction. If the process crashes or an exception occurs after `revise!` commits but before `update_column` succeeds, the post content can be updated while `topic_embeds.content_sha1` remains stale. Subsequent imports will keep seeing a mismatch and repeatedly re-run `revise!` even when no further changes exist. This lack of atomicity is verifiable from the diff (create path uses a transaction; update path does not).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — The return value of @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) is never checked before continuing to save_reply_relationships and returning true from revise!, so a failed save is silently treated as success

adjudication.rationale: In lib/post_revisor.rb `update_post` calls `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` and ignores the boolean return value, then unconditionally calls `@post.save_reply_relationships`. Since `save` can return `false` (validation failure when `skip_validations` is not set, or DB-level failure), this code path can continue as if the post persisted successfully, potentially leaving reply relationships inconsistent with the unsaved post changes. The diff does not add any error handling/checking for the save result.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — X-Frame-Options is unconditionally set to ALLOWALL once the spoofable referer check passes, removing clickjacking protection for the embed pages for any client that forges a matching Referer
matched_golden_ids: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that X-Frame-Options is set to ALLOWALL (disabling clickjacking protection) and that the Referer-based gating is spoofable/bypassable by forging a matching Referer. This aligns with the golden issue’s core concerns, though it doesn’t explicitly mention the nil-referer empty-string fallback masking failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — TopicEmbed.import_remote is called with an import-file-controlled URL (t[:link]); import_remote itself has no host allow-list (that check only lives in TopicRetriever, a different caller), so this path's open(url) fetch is unrestricted SSRF surface

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the import task now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` immediately does `open(url).read` (via open-uri) with no host allow-list or scheme restriction. The host check exists only in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, but that is not used on this code path. Although `TopicEmbed.import` later rejects non-`http(s)` URLs, the network/file fetch already occurred in `import_remote`, so a crafted `t[:link]` in the import data can trigger unrestricted outbound requests (and potentially local file reads for non-http schemes) when an admin runs the task, which is a verifiable SSRF surface introduced by this diff.
